examples.title: Working together
examples.problem: A and B together can do a job in 10 days, B and C in 12 days, and C and A in 15 days. How long will A, B and C take working together?
steps: Each person is counted twice in that sum, so the three together do half of it: 1/8 of the job a day.
So A, B and C together take 8 days.

examples.title: Pipes and cisterns
examples.problem: A pipe can fill a tank in 9 hours. Because of a leak at the bottom, it actually takes 12 hours to fill. How long would the leak take to empty the full tank?
steps: With the leak, the net rate is 1/12 of the tank an hour.
Leak rate = 1/9 − 1/12 = (4 − 3)/36 = 1/36 of the tank an hour.
So the leak empties the full tank in 36 hours.

examples.title: Men, days and hours
examples.problem: Twenty workers, working 8 hours a day, finish a job in 15 days. How many days will 25 workers take if they work 6 hours a day?
steps: 25 workers at 6 hours a day give 25 × 6 = 150 worker-hours a day.

examples.title: Efficiency and wages
examples.problem: A is 25% more efficient than B. They do a job together and are paid ₹7,200, shared in proportion to the work each does. How much does A get?
steps: A's efficiency is 1.25 times B's, so the ratio of their efficiencies is 5 : 4.
Both work for the same number of days, so the work they do is also in the ratio 5 : 4.

examples.title: Alternate days
examples.problem: A can do a job in 6 days and B in 9 days. They work on alternate days, starting with A. In how many days is the job done?
steps: Take the job as 18 units: A does 3 a day and B does 2.
Each 2-day cycle finishes 5 units, so 3 cycles (6 days) finish 15 units.
On day 7 A does 3 more units, which completes the 18.
